nodes.summary: Containing $T^*$ as a subtournament. A relation $T$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ contains $T^*$ when there is an injective map $f$ from the vertex set $\{0, \dots, 5\}$ of $T^*$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that for all vertices $i, j$ of $T^*$, $i \to j$ in $T^*$ if and only if $T(f(i), f(j))$ holds.
nodes.title: Containing $T^*$ as a subtournament

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A relation $T$ on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is a tournament when $T(x, x)$ holds for no $x$ and, for all distinct $x$ and $y$, exactly one of $T(x, y)$ and $T(y, x)$ holds.
nodes.title: Tournaments

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $T$ be a relation on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $S$ be a set of its elements. Then $T$ is transitive on $S$ when, for all $x, y, z \in S$, $T(x, y)$ and $T(y, z)$ imply $T(x, z)$. For a tournament $T$ this says that the subtournament of $T$ on $S$ is transitive.
nodes.title: Transitivity on a vertex set

nodes.summary: The backward arcs of $T^*$. The list of ordered pairs $(5, 0)$, $(5, 2)$, $(4, 1)$, $(3, 0)$ of vertices in $\{0, \dots, 5\}$. These are the arcs of the six-vertex tournament $T^*$ that go from a larger to a smaller vertex: $6 \to 1$, $6 \to 3$, $5 \to 2$ and $4 \to 1$ in the source's labelling $1, \dots, 6$, with every vertex lowered by one.
nodes.title: The backward arcs of $T^*$

nodes.summary: Nguyen–Scott–Seymour: $T^*$ has the Erdős–Hajnal property. There is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every tournament $T$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that does not contain $T^*$ as a subtournament, there is a set $S$ of vertices on which $T$ is transitive with $|S| \ge n^{\varepsilon}$.
nodes.title: Nguyen–Scott–Seymour: $T^*$ has the Erdős–Hajnal property

nodes.summary: The Erdős–Hajnal problem for the tournament $T^*$. There is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every tournament $T$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that does not contain $T^*$ as a subtournament, there is a set $S$ of vertices on which $T$ is transitive with $|S| \ge n^{\varepsilon}$.
nodes.title: The Erdős–Hajnal problem for the tournament $T^*$

nodes.summary: The six-vertex tournament $T^*$. The tournament $T^*$ is the relation on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, 5\}$ with an arc $i \to j$ if and only if either $(i, j)$ is one of the backward arcs $(5, 0)$, $(5, 2)$, $(4, 1)$, $(3, 0)$, or $i < j$ and $(j, i)$ is not a backward arc.
nodes.title: The six-vertex tournament $T^*$

nodes.summary: It is not the case that $f(n) = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$ for every $n \ge 1$, where $f(n)$ is the largest $m$ such that every tournament on $n$ vertices contains a transitive subtournament on $m$ vertices.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1216 is false

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, $f(n) = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$, where $f(n)$ is the largest $m$ such that every tournament on $n$ vertices contains a transitive subtournament on $m$ vertices.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1216 (the Erdős–Moser formula)

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f(n)$ is the largest $m$ such that every tournament $T$ on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is transitive on some set of exactly $m$ vertices, that is, contains a transitive subtournament on $m$ vertices.
nodes.title: Transitive subtournament number

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
